plan: Keep all patient-facing state in the single public `session` dict, with one canonical initial-state constant reused by construction, `begin`, and `abandon` so reset semantics stay identical.
Dispatch `handle` through a table mapping the six action types to handler methods; anything else (non-dict action, unknown type) short-circuits to an error screen.

Use validate-then-commit in every handler: check activity/completion guards and field types/values first, return an `Error:` screen on any failure, and mutate `session` only after all checks pass so invalid actions never corrupt accepted data and never raise.

Derive prompts from state: fixed prompts for begin/choice/complete/abandon, and a `_next_prompt()` unmet-requirement scan (contact -> appointment -> review) for corrections, matching the ordering `complete` enforces.

Route every screen through one `_screen` factory that builds the exact {prompt, messages, choices} shape and attaches appointment choices (in input order, as fresh {id, label} dicts) exactly when the prompt is `Choose appointment`.

Inject `action_source` and `screen_sink` as duck-typed collaborators; `run_once` raises RuntimeError before touching either if one is missing, then does read_action -> handle -> display exactly once and returns the same screen object, so unittest.mock or hand-written stdlib fakes drop in directly.
Shallow-copy the appointments sequence and its dicts at construction so caller-side mutation cannot affect emitted choices.
mechanisms: single-source-of-truth session dict with canonical initial-state constant
validate-then-commit guards producing Error: screens without mutation
centralized screen factory enforcing the choices/prompt invariant
constructor-injected source/sink ports with fail-fast RuntimeError in run_once
